answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by pricing identity with a refundable bond. Each new agent must lock collateral to enter the harbor as a peer, so free duplicate names buy nothing. An attacker seeking a thousand votes must post a thousand bonds, making the cost grow linearly with every fake identity. Caught fraud triggers slashing, a ripple that wipes all of that attacker's stakes at once. The velvet gate stays cheap for honest agents who reclaim their bond, but is costly for anyone mass producing sybils.
